prompt.en: A CW exciter is rebuilt so the buffer has much better reverse isolation. When the following RF amplifier input load swings during keying, what should happen to oscillator pulling?

text.en: Pulling should increase because reverse isolation adds extra RF output power
Pulling should decrease because less of the load change reaches the oscillator
Pulling should stay the same because buffers only shape key-click envelopes
The oscillator should jump to a harmonic because isolation acts like a multiplier

explanation.en: Better reverse isolation makes the buffer more one-way, so load changes in the RF amplifier are less able to tug the oscillator frequency.

prompt.en: An SSB exciter has a filtered signal at 9.000 MHz and mixes it with a 5.250 MHz VFO using the sum product. What output frequency is produced before final amplification?

explanation.en: For the sum product, add the two frequencies: 9.000 MHz + 5.250 MHz = 14.250 MHz.

prompt.en: Spot the error in this receiver troubleshooting note: “The selected IF signal is present, so turning up AF gain will let the product detector recover SSB even if its local reference is absent.”

text.en: The antenna must be disconnected before any product detector can recover audio
The sideband filter belongs after the speaker whenever AF gain is increased
The local oscillator should be mixed with the AF output instead of with the incoming RF signal
AF gain after the detector cannot replace the local reference needed to mix the selected IF into audio

explanation.en: The product detector has to combine selected IF energy with a nearby reference before the AF amplifier can raise the recovered audio level.
